hook.text: A pipeline lands raw tables in the warehouse. A dashboard shows revenue. Between the two sits a layer of models, and an analytics engineer owns it.

hook-more.text: Raw tables go in; clean, tested, documented models come out, usually built with dbt. The role sits between data engineering and analytics.

probe-model.text: SQL and modeling: facts and dimensions, star schemas, the grain, and slowly changing dimensions.
probe-model.spoken: Sequel and modeling: facts and dimensions, star schemas, the grain, and slowly changing dimensions.

probe-dbt.text: Then dbt itself: models, refs and sources, tests, materializations and documentation.

probe-practice.text: Software practice: version control, continuous integration, layers from staging to marts, and SQL that doesn't repeat itself.
probe-practice.spoken: Software practice: version control, continuous integration, layers from staging to marts, and sequel that doesn't repeat itself.

probe-tradeoffs.text: And trade-offs: a view, a table or an incremental model, and cost against freshness.

ai.text: AI has added to that core, not replaced it. Modeling, dbt and SQL still come first.
ai.spoken: AI has added to that core, not replaced it. Modeling, dbt and sequel still come first.

ai-why.text: What's new is a reader. Companies put ask-your-data assistants in front of their warehouses, and an assistant is only as reliable as the metric definitions underneath it. Those are an analytics engineer's work.

ai-sql.text: Why text-to-SQL over raw tables gives confident wrong answers, and how a semantic layer prevents them.
ai-sql.spoken: Why text-to-sequel over raw tables gives confident wrong answers, and how a semantic layer prevents them.

ai-ready.text: AI-ready modeling: documentation, tests and access rules written for a reader that is a language model.

ai-eval.text: Evaluating an assistant against answers you've verified, including questions it should decline.

ai-review.text: And reviewing a dbt model an assistant wrote, for its grain, its incremental logic and duplicate metrics.

ai-ask.text: Some coding rounds allow an assistant, so ask the recruiter about each round.

ai-more.text: Part nine covers all four in depth.

series.text: This series argues modeling decisions, and the ways they fail. Code comes on screen only as evidence.

practice.text: Every topic page has concept checks, three of them add challenges that run in the browser, and a bank of a hundred and ten multiple-choice questions covers the whole track.
